items.title: Film promotion cancelled at Chennai’s Phoenix mall after chaos erupts from overcrowding
items.summary: Follow TNM’s WhatsApp channel for news updates and story links. Mishaps arising from overcrowding were averted at the Phoenix Marketcity mall in Chennai's Velachery on Saturday, August 8, after thousands of people gathered for a promotional event of the movie Meesaya Murukku 2 . The police cancelled the programme amid concerns of public safety and potential chaos. The non-ticketed event, organised at the mall for actor and musician Hiphop Tamizha Aadhi’s upcoming film, was expected to draw around 1,000 people, according to the police. However, a much larger crowd turned up after social media posts reportedly described the programme as a free musical event featuring Aadhi's performance. By Saturday evening, more than 2,000 people were reportedly gathered, with a large number of them thronging around the stage area. Police warned that the situation could lead to untoward incidents and advised Aadhi not to proceed with the event. The situation also triggered severe traffic congestion across Velachery and surrounding areas, with motorists stuck for several hours. items.summary: The Mumbai police arrested a former student of the Tata Institute of Social Sciences (TISS) on the night of Friday, August 7, shortly after a Sessions Court refused to grant him pre-arrest bail. The police arrested 32-year-old Abhirup Paul in Chembur in connection with an FIR filed by the institute over a 2025 memorial event held for late Delhi University professor GN Saibaba, who died on October 12, 2024, shortly after his acquittal in a case under the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA). Saibaba’s death was attributed to the severe deterioration of his health during the prolonged incarceration. Of the nine students booked in the case, two — Kamakhya Prasad Das, 23, from Assam, and Abhirup Paul, 32 — were denied pre-arrest bail by the Mumbai Sessions Court, which said they had failed to show “respect for the law of the land”. While Abhirup has been arrested, Kamakhya Prasad is yet to be taken into custody, police said, according to The Indian Express. The police reportedly sought 10 days of custody for Abhirup, but the court granted custody until Monday, August 10. items.title: Immediate FIR mandatory for missing adults too: Supreme Court clarifies order, warns States of contempt
items.summary: The Supreme Court has clarified that its direction requiring immediate registration of first information reports (FIRs) on receiving information about a missing person applies to adults as well as children, irrespective of age or gender. [G Ganesh v. State of Tamil Nadu & Ors] In an order passed on August 5, a Bench of Justices Ahsanuddin Amanullah and R Mahadevan expressed shock that some States had understood the expression "person" in its earlier order to refer only to children. " We find this to be a deliberate and mala fide bogey raised by such States. The language of our earlier order is clear and unambiguous. The expression 'person' means every person, irrespective of age or gender, " the Court said. Justices Ahsanuddin Amanullah and R Mahadevan The Bench was referring to its May 22 order directing States to register an FIR upon receiving information regarding any missing person. It warned that if any State or Union Territory (UT) has failed to comply with the direction in its true letter and spirit, a contempt notice would be issued to the concerned Chief Secretary and Director General of Police (DGP). items.title: Supreme Court rejects TV Today's challenge to ₹5 lakh compensation for violating child sexual abuse victim's privacy
items.summary: The Supreme Court today dismissed a plea filed by TV Today, which operates Aaj Tak, challenging the Delhi High Court's directive that it to pay ₹5 lakhs as compensation for violating the privacy of a child sexual abuse survivor by broadcasting details that exposed her identity [ TV Today Network Limited v. ABC ]. A Bench of Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana dismissed the plea. Justice Joymalya Bagchi, CJI Surya Kant and Justice V Mohana The case concerned an incident from a 2005 incident in which a minor girl lodged an FIR against her father alleging sexual assault. It was stated that after the child's mother refused to allow Aaj Tak's crew to interview her or her daughter, the channel nevertheless aired a report containing the father's name, designation and workplace, visuals of the family's residential colony and house, and the mother's voice. The victim’s mother filed a writ petition against the channel in 2005 and in 2013, a single-judge allowed the plea and awarded damages of ₹5 lakh in favour of the child’s mother.
